heading: Orange, red alerts for A.P. as depression in Bay is likely to bring heavy rain in next three days
author: The Hindu Bureau
paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has issued orange alerts for the northern districts of Andhra Pradesh for September 22 as the well-marked low pressure area over Bay of Bengal has intensified into a depression on Monday.

According to the weather forecast, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at one or two places in the districts of Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, ASR, Anakapalli and Kakinada on Tuesday.

The intensity of rainfall will increase on September 23, 24 and 25 when the system is likely to intesify further. Except for Rayalaseema, all the other districts are expected to receive widespread or fairly widespread rainfall on these three days. Red alerts have been issued for the districts of Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna and Eluru on September 23 and 24 as extremely heavy rainfall is expected at one or two places in the districts on these two days.
The other coastal and northern districts have been put on orange alert while no such alerts have been given for the eight districts of Rayalaseema.

According to the bulletin from the IMD, the well-marked low-pressure area intensified into a depression and lay centred over west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal, which is around 310 km southeast of Puri in Odisha, 390 km east-southeast of Kalingapatnam of A.P. and 470 km east of Visakhapatnam. The system is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression by Tuesday. Continuing to move west-northwestwards, it is very likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur as a deep depression around September 24.

On Monday, between 8.30 a.m. and 6 p.m., Sankhavaram in Kakinada received the day’s highest of 60.75 mm, followed by Nandaluru in NTR district with 52.5 mm, Peddapuram in Kakinada 48.25 mm, Durvesi in Nandyal 45.5 mm, Kavvuluru in NTR district 45.36 mm, Ramakuppam in Chittoor district 39.31 mm, and D. Hirehal in Anantapur 35.5 mm. Many other stations in the districts of Anakapalli, Srikakulam, Chittoor, Nandyal, NTR, Markapuram, and SPSR Nellore received light to moderate showers.
The A.P. State Disaster Management Authority has warned fishermen against going into the sea as it is expected to remain rough for the next four days.
